items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: my piano player was John Malachi.

ctx.x: I don't know. I'd have to go back and find that year when it was. But I had a little band at the Yacht Club on 52nd Street, and my piano player was John Malachi. My bass player was Tommy Potter. I got them out of Washington. And they went with Billy Eckstine later on, the
two of them with Billy Eckstine's big band. But I can't -- I couldn't tell you the year. I really couldn't tell you.

items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: While I was still here, I started writing these arrangements for Trummy, and he stayed down here and we duplicated some or most of those arrangements.

ctx.x: What happened was, I turned the band over to Leonard Phillips, and it later became Phil Phillips' band. I gave him all the arrangements that I had everything.

So we got this little band together... While I was still here, I started writing these arrangements for Trummy, and he stayed down here and we duplicated some or most of those arrangements. We did "Margie" and "Down By The Old Mill Stream" -- some of the popular Jimmy Lunceford things. When we felt like the band was ready, we were rehearsed and everything, Trummy set this gig up and said we were going...
